Ashkenazi Synagogue in Rome

Synagogue · Lazio, Italy

Agudat Ashkenazim is an active Orthodox synagogue in central Rome, located near Termini railway station. The congregation follows the Ashkenazi *nusach* and serves local residents, students, and Jewish travelers visiting the city.

Rome is home to one of Europe’s oldest continuous Jewish communities, historically shaped by the distinctive Italian rite as well as Sephardic traditions. The city’s Ashkenazi community grew significantly during the 20th century, as Jews from Germany, Austria, and Eastern Europe settled in Italy and established congregations to preserve their own religious customs and liturgy. Agudat Ashkenazim remains an important expression of this heritage within Rome’s diverse Jewish community.

Visitor information:

Weekday morning services are generally held Sunday through Friday at 7:40, while Shabbat morning services usually begin at 10:00 and are followed by Kiddush. The synagogue may be closed on some Shabbatot in August. Visitors are advised to contact the congregation in advance to confirm service times and arrange any required security clearance.
